summary: Esho Sasaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Sasaki held academic posts at Ikenobo Junior College as an associate professor and at Kyoto Women's University as a professor.

Esho Yamaguchi specialized in Indology and philosophy, studying at Kyoto University from circa 1939 to 1944. Yamaguchi served as a professor at Osaka University from circa 1962 to 1982 and held a post at Ritsumeikan University from circa 1982 to 1989.

Eshō Mikogami was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who founded Indogaku Chibettogaku Kenkyū in 1996. Mikogami served as a professor at Ryukoku University (1963–2003), headed the Ryukoku Association of Buddhist Studies (1997), and was a professor at Otani University (~1989–2005).

Ester Bianchi is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD studying at Ca' Foscari University of Venice and École Pratique des Hautes Études under Jean-Noël Robert and Alfredo Cadonna, later holding posts at the University of Florence and University of Perugia.

Etsuaki Teraishi works in the fields of Indology and philosophy. Teraishi has held appointments as a special research fellow at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science and as an associate professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College.

Eugen Hultzsch was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under Georg Bühler from circa 1880 to 1882. From circa 1886 to 1903, he served as an epigraphist for the Government of Madras, the Archaeological Survey of India, and the Government of India.

Eugen Pander was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who studied at Polytechnikum Riga from circa 1873 to 1877. In 1881, he served as a professor of economics and lecturer in Russian and German at Tongwen Guan.

Eugen Wilhelm was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied under August Schleicher from circa 1860 to 1864 and served as a professor at the University of Jena from circa 1869 to 1923.

Eugene Watson Burlingame was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Charles Rockwell Lanman. He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~1908–1913), Johns Hopkins University (~1913–1917), and Yale University (~1917–1932).

Eugene Y. Wang is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who studied under Wu Hung and John M. Rosenfield. He held a post at the University of Chicago (~1996–1997) and became Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Professor of Asian Art at Harvard University in ~2005.

Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lviv University (~1919–1924). He held posts at Lviv University (~1931–1939), Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń (~1945–1953), and served as head of Indology at the University of Warsaw (~1953–1971).

Eugène Burnouf was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He held positions at the École Normale Supérieure (1829), Société Asiatique (1826–1852), Imprimerie Nationale (~1832–1852), and Collège de France (1832–1852).
Eugène Jacquet was a scholar in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat from circa 1829 to 1832 and under Eugène Burnouf from circa 1832 to 1838.

Eugène Obermiller was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky. From circa 1930 to 1935, he held posts at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts and as Section Secretary at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Eun-su Cho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. Cho served as an assistant professor at the University of Michigan (1997–2004) and became professor of Buddhist philosophy at Seoul National University in 2004.
Eunyoung Choi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Korea University by 2007. In circa 2008, Choi took up an HK Professor post at Geumgang University.

Eva K. Neumaier is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1957–1966). She served at the University of Alberta (~1991–2003) as chair and professor, and as Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary (~1999–2000).
Eva K. Neumaier-Dargyay is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Khenpo Rigzin. She held an academic post at the University of Calgary from circa 1980 to 1991.

Evan Thompson is a philosopher who studied at Amherst College and the University of Toronto under Robert A. F. Thurman and Francisco Varela. He held posts at Tufts, Boston University, Concordia, Colorado Boulder, École Polytechnique, York University, University of Toronto, and University of British Columbia.

Eviatar Shulman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from circa 1998 to 2008, where he also held a Mandel postdoctoral fellowship at the Scholion center in 2009.
